problem: It is challenging to build QA systems that learn to reason over knowledge graphs from question-answer pairs alone due to noisy question expressions and the need for multi-hop logic reasoning.
method: Proposes a novel unified deep learning architecture and an end-to-end variational learning algorithm that handles noise in questions and learns multi-hop reasoning simultaneously.
key_assumptions: Variational inference can effectively model uncertainty in question expressions and multi-hop reasoning.
The unified architecture can jointly handle noise and learn reasoning.
main_contribution: A unified deep learning architecture with variational learning achieving state-of-the-art performance on a recent benchmark dataset, plus new benchmark datasets for multi-hop reasoning, paraphrased questions, and human voice questions.
datasets: derived benchmark datasets: questions for multi-hop reasoning, questions paraphrased by neural translation model, questions in human voice
results: ["state-of-the-art performance on the recent benchmark dataset; very promising results on derived datasets"]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: The paper uses a variational learning algorithm for noise handling and multi-hop reasoning, whereas the idea enriches target triples with local context subgraphs from source passages, adds an adaptive repair loop for factual reliability, and applies RL transfer from lower-hop QA.
